# Translate a Foreign-Language Message in Messenger with Meta AI

> **In short:** Open the Messenger chat, mention @Meta AI, and ask it to translate the message. It replies in plain English right under your request — no copy-pasting. It works best for short, casual messages; long technical texts may need a second pass.

You know the feeling: someone sends a message in Spanish, Japanese, or German, and you stare at it for ten seconds trying to sound out a word. With Meta AI (Meta's built-in assistant, available inside Messenger in many regions) sitting right inside your chats, you can get a translation in seconds without leaving the conversation. Here's how to do it on your phone, step by step.

## Before you start
- **The Messenger app** on iPhone or Android — the latest version is best, because older versions may not show Meta AI yet.
- **A Meta account** (the same one you use for Facebook or Instagram).
- **A chat with at least one foreign-language message** in it — ideally with someone who can confirm the translation.
- **Roughly 2 minutes.** That's the whole thing.

## Step 1 — Open the chat with the foreign-language message
Tap the Messenger icon on your phone and find the conversation with the message you can't read. Open it. You'll see the chat fill the screen, scroll to the newest messages, and show the foreign-language text in its bubble near the bottom. The message is right there — you don't have to dig for it. If you have lots of chats, use the search bar at the top of Messenger and type the person's name to jump straight in.

💬 Example: a Spanish message that says *"Oye, podemos vernos mañana a las 5?"* (you don't know what it means yet).

You'll know it worked when the chat screen takes over your phone and you can see the unread message sitting in its bubble.

## Step 2 — Bring Meta AI into the chat
Tap the message text box at the bottom — the one you normally type replies into — and type **@Meta AI**. A small list of suggestions should pop up; look for one labeled **Meta AI** and tap it to invite the assistant into the chat. If @Meta AI doesn't appear as a suggestion, your app may be on an older version, or Meta AI may not be available in your region yet — in that case, update Messenger from your app store and try again. On some versions you'll also see a colorful ring or circle labeled **Meta AI** near the top of the chat; tapping that works the same way.

💬 Example: type `@Meta AI` and tap the Meta AI suggestion from the pop-up list.

You'll know it worked when a small "Meta AI" chip appears next to your message, or when Meta AI posts a welcome reply in the chat.

## Step 3 — Ask Meta AI to translate the message
With @Meta AI now part of the conversation, type your translation request in plain English. Mention the language if you know it, and quote the original message so the AI knows exactly what to translate. Press send. Meta AI replies in the same chat thread — you don't have to switch screens or open a new tab. Keep your request short and direct; the clearer your instruction, the better the translation usually is.

💬 Example: `@Meta AI translate this to English: "Oye, podemos vernos mañana a las 5?"`

You'll know it worked when Meta AI posts a reply in English within a few seconds, right under your message.

## Step 4 — Read the translation and check it makes sense
Read Meta AI's reply carefully. Short, everyday sentences usually translate cleanly. Watch out for slang, idioms, or proper names — AI translations sometimes miss those, or pick the wrong meaning for a word with several. If the translation looks odd or incomplete, your next move is Step 5. If it reads naturally, you're done — go ahead and reply to your friend in English, or use Step 5 to ask for a draft reply in their language.

💬 Example: Meta AI's reply reads *"Hey, can we meet tomorrow at 5?"* — that one is smooth and obvious in meaning.

You'll know it worked when you understand what the original message meant and can decide how to respond.

## Step 5 — Ask a follow-up if the translation is unclear
If the first translation is confusing, too formal, or missing a word, send a follow-up message to Meta AI in the same chat. Ask for a simpler version, a different tone, or just for the meaning of one specific word. Meta AI keeps the context of the conversation, so it can adjust without starting over. If you'd like, you can also ask Meta AI to help you write a reply in the foreign language — copy what it drafts, edit if needed, and send it to your friend.

💬 Example: `@Meta AI can you make that sound more casual?` or `@Meta AI what does "mañana" mean on its own?`

You'll know it worked when the new reply reads more clearly, or when you have a draft reply in the original language to send back.

## Common mistakes
- **Forgetting to type @Meta AI.** If you just type "translate this" without the @ mention, your message goes to your friend, not the AI. Always start your request with `@Meta AI`.
- **Asking Meta AI to translate a very long paragraph.** Short messages translate cleanly; long blocks can lose nuance or drop words. For long or important texts, use a dedicated translation tool or ask a native speaker.
- **Trusting the translation for anything high-stakes.** Meta AI is great for casual chats, but for legal, medical, or business messages, double-check with a native speaker or a professional translator before acting on it.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** the next time a relative abroad sends a quick message, you'll know what it says in seconds — and you can reply right away instead of leaving them on read.
- **For your business or work:** if a colleague or client messages you in another language, you can keep the conversation moving in Messenger instead of juggling translation apps and copy-paste.
- **If you're just getting started:** try it once this week with any short message in a language you don't speak. Two minutes, and you'll have it down for life.

## Try it now
Open Messenger, pick the most recent chat with a message you can't quite read, and type `@Meta AI translate this to English` followed by the message. See what comes back — that's the whole skill.
